newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Contact group rules out sanctions on Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Contact group rules out sanctions on Serbia.

text.p: A high level Contact Group on former Yugoslavia on Saturday ruled out imposing sanctions against Serbia in order to pressure President Slobodan Milosevic into acknowledging opposition success in local elections.
"The general consensus is that we are not at the point to pursue sanctions," said U.S. Secretary of State for Europe John Kornblum after a meeting of the group in Brussels.

The Contact Group -- made up of senior officials from the U.S, Britain, Germany, France, Italy and Russia -- was meeting to discuss ways of putting pressure on Belgrade to accept a report by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

The report, compiled by former Spanish Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez, says the Serbian opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition won 14 of 18 cities, including Belgrade, in recent municipal elections. Serbian authorities annulled the victories.
"The feeling is that we should continue with diplomatic pressure at this time," Kornblum said. "Sanctions will not resolve the present crisis in Yugoslavia."

Kornblum said however that individual countries were independently examining ways of applying pressure on Milosevic and the U.S. was considering unilaterally freezing trade and official relations with Serbia.
